purpose: Bind the primary research hypothesis to a fixed geometric coupling plane at the bottom of the SWAP profile, separating interface hydraulic head from SWAP phreatic elevation and separating physical/mathematical proof from numerical proof.

evidence: src/runtime/mod_fmr_groundwater_head_forcing_adapter.f90 maps interface hydraulic head to SWAP bottom_head only for bottom_mode=5.
src/runtime/mod_modflow6_swap_prescribed_qbot_bottom_face.f90 defines the predictor state as a lower coupling-plane hydraulic head and explicitly states that it is not the freatic groundwater level.
integration/research/GC_REAL_SWAP_MAP11_RESULT.json does not establish coextensive SWAP/MODFLOW storage.
integration/research/GC_REAL_SWAP_MAP12_LEGACY_HEAD_SEMANTICS_AUDIT.json distinguishes mode-5 lower-face head from legacy mode-1 prescribed groundwater level.
current_production_observation.nonclaim: This classification describes the current bounded route. It is not a recommendation that the final architecture remain in this family.
current_production_observation.limit_to_shared_phreatic: Only in a separately demonstrated hydrostatic/vanishing vertical-resistance state limit with consistent storage ownership; head equality alone is insufficient.

SHARED_PHREATIC.physical_state: one phreatic elevation H plus SWAP internal state
SHARED_PHREATIC.exchange: no physical resistance between duplicate phreatic heads; internal bookkeeping transfers cancel from the complete system
SHARED_PHREATIC.discriminant: requires explicit coextensive/shared-state geometry and one combined storage law

INTERFACE_SPLIT.physical_state: shared/interface hydraulic head at a geometric coupling plane; phreatic elevation may be a different SWAP state under vertical gradient
INTERFACE_SPLIT.physical_storage: SWAP and MODFLOW own disjoint geometric control volumes
INTERFACE_SPLIT.exchange: physical interface flux with equal and opposite component accounting; may be solved by iterated head/flux boundary exchange
INTERFACE_SPLIT.discriminant: requires a declared coupling plane and a justified mapping from MODFLOW representative head to interface head

FINITE_RESISTANCE_QLINK.discriminant: requires physical evidence for both states and the resistance; coefficient dimensions alone are insufficient

invalid_shortcut.description: Two model components both count the full storage response of the same physical volume.
invalid_shortcut.evidence: DSW01/DSW02/DSW19; later DSW23/HLINK01 are supporting mechanism evidence within their recorded qualification bounds.
invalid_shortcut.consequence: Numerical bookkeeping can close while the one-volume physical head response is wrong.

required_questions: What is the SWAP physical control volume?
What is the MODFLOW physical control volume?
What exactly is the exchanged head: phreatic elevation, interface hydraulic head, MODFLOW cell representative head, or another state?
Is there one physical head state or two?
If there are two states, what physical law determines exchange?
Which storage-volume change belongs to each control volume?
Which fluxes are external to the complete system and which are internal?
Which SWAP internal states must persist even if one head is shared?
Which derivative is needed for the nonlinear algorithm, separately from the physical quantity it linearizes?
architecture_gate: No production change is authorized. First derive the fixed-interface equations independently of u/q_u and HCOF/RHS; then test whether the current response condensation is algebraically and numerically consistent with those equations.
next_scientific_step: Derive and preregister a minimal nonhydrostatic analytical fixed-interface case in which interface head H_c and SWAP phreatic elevation are deliberately different, before implementing the numerical test.

original_thought_experiment.reason: The simple control can make interface hydraulic head and SWAP phreatic elevation numerically equal. That equality is a hydrostatic limiting result and must not be promoted to semantic identity.
original_thought_experiment.exact_oracle: 0.010 m / 0.20 = 0.050 m head rise, final shared head 8.05 m from an 8.00 m origin.
original_thought_experiment.nonclaim: The control does not establish that MODFLOW computes the SWAP phreatic elevation; the next discriminating oracle must impose vertical resistance/gradient so H_c and z_phreatic differ.

primary_contract.coupling_plane: fixed elevation z_c at the lower boundary of the SWAP profile
primary_contract.state_semantics: H_c is interface hydraulic head, not a MODFLOW-computed phreatic groundwater elevation
primary_contract.swap_role: given H_c and committed SWAP state/forcing, resolve the top-system state, phreatic elevation, storage/process response and bottom-interface exchange
primary_contract.modflow_role: solve groundwater hydraulic head including H_c at the declared coupling plane/cell representation; do not reinterpret H_c as phreatic elevation by definition
primary_contract.hydrostatic_limit: H_c may numerically equal the SWAP phreatic elevation in a hydrostatic/high-conductivity control, but this is a limiting result rather than state identity
primary_contract.nonhydrostatic_requirement: The proof programme must include a regime with H_c != z_phreatic while interface head and flux continuity and complete mass closure remain correct.

proof_layers: PHYSICAL_CONCEPTUAL: define geometry, control volumes, states, storage ownership and flux ownership
MATHEMATICAL: derive component balances, complete balance, interface conditions and coupled residual
NUMERICAL_CORRECTNESS: show the implemented u/q_u, HCOF/RHS and iteration solve the derived equations
NUMERICAL_QUALITY: separately assess convergence, robustness, timestep and tolerance envelope
